title: Best Data Removal Services: DeleteMe vs Incogni & More
metaDescription: Compare data removal services DeleteMe, Incogni, Kanary and Privacy Bee on broker coverage, reporting, support and refund terms.
intro: Data brokers profit billions from selling your personal information without consent. Manual opt-outs are time-consuming and often ineffective. These data removal services automate the process, continuously monitoring and removing your data from hundreds of broker sites.

verdict.summary: DeleteMe, Incogni and Privacy Bee tie for the highest score on this table (listed alphabetically). DeleteMe offers email, chat and phone support and a detailed report every quarter, and says it covers 750+ broker sites, many through custom requests, but its full refund applies only before the first report. Incogni handles 420+ brokers automatically, costs $95.88 a year for Standard and has a 30-day money-back guarantee. Privacy Bee lists 517 brokers on Essentials and 1,100+ on Pro, sends monthly progress reports and offers a 30-day guarantee on those two plans. Kanary is just behind; it also covers search engines, though two of its rows could not be assessed from public information. None of these services publishes independently verified removal success rates, so that row is not scored.

pro_tips: Search for your own listings in a private window while signed out, so the searches aren't saved to your accounts or browser history.
Start with one service for 6 months, then check if your data reappears before committing long-term - some brokers re-add information.
Keep records of your own opt-out attempts before using a service - you can provide this list to speed up the removal process.
Set up Google Alerts for your name and address to monitor when new data appears online between service scans.
Consider using a dedicated email address for the data removal service to track all removal confirmations and avoid inbox clutter.

faqs.question: How long does it take to see results from data removal services?
faqs.answer: Most services begin removing your data within 7-10 days, but complete removal from all targeted sites typically takes 2-3 months. Some stubborn brokers may take up to 6 months to fully comply with removal requests.

faqs.question: Will my data stay removed permanently?
faqs.answer: No, data removal is an ongoing process. Brokers often re-add information from new sources, which is why these services keep checking and re-sending removal requests on a schedule. DeleteMe reports quarterly and Kanary monthly.

faqs.question: Can I remove my data from brokers myself for free?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it takes time. Each broker has its own opt-out process, many relist people later, and covering dozens of brokers can take many hours plus regular re-checks. Paid services send the requests and do the re-checks for you.

faqs.question: Do these services work for family members too?
faqs.answer: Yes, several do. DeleteMe sells couple and family plans (up to 4 people), Incogni has family plans for up to 5 people, and Kanary adds family members at half price. Each person usually still needs to provide their own details, because removal requests are made in their name.

faqs.question: What's the difference between data removal services and identity theft protection?
faqs.answer: Data removal services proactively remove your information from broker sites to prevent exposure. Identity theft protection monitors for misuse after exposure has already occurred. Some companies sell bundles that include both, so check what a plan actually covers.

faqs.question: Are there any risks to using data removal services?
faqs.answer: The main risk is providing personal information to the service itself. Choose established companies with clear privacy policies. Also, some removals might affect legitimate services like background checks for employment or housing applications.
